hints: Look closely at what the chromosomes are doing in each numbered cell: are they a tangled ball, thick separate threads, lined up in the middle, pulled apart, or in two separate groups?
Remember the mitosis order is prophase (condensing), then metaphase (line up on equator), then anaphase (sister chromatids pulled apart), then telophase (two groups reforming nuclei).
walkthrough:
**Identify what each numbered cell shows**

Look at the chromosome pattern first, it tells you the stage. Cell 3 has a tangled mass of thin condensing chromatin. Cell 1 has thicker, shorter, more distinct chromosomes. Cell 4 has chromosomes lined up in a row. Cell 5 has V-shaped chromatids moving apart. Cell 2 has two separate groups at opposite ends.

**Put them in mitosis order**

Prophase comes first, so the tangled ball in 3 is earliest, followed by the clearer chromosomes in 1 as late prophase. Then metaphase is lining up on the equator, so 4 is next. Then anaphase is separation, so 5 is next. Then telophase is two groups, so 2 is last.

**Choose the matching sequence**

That gives the order:
$$3 \rightarrow 1 \rightarrow 4 \rightarrow 5 \rightarrow 2$$
This matches option C exactly.

options.A: Starts with 1 before 3, but 3 is earlier prophase with less condensed chromatin than 1.
options.B: Starts with 1 before 3 and puts 2 last after 5 incorrectly, 2 is telophase with two groups so it must be last.
options.C: Correct order: 3 early prophase, 1 late prophase, 4 metaphase, 5 anaphase, 2 telophase.
options.D: Puts 4 before 1, but 1 (prophase chromosomes) must come before 4 (metaphase plate).
